parsed.modern: To the arches GF, CB, draw the tangents HF, OB, and the sines CM G and the radii DP DB; and draw list the sine of the arch AB, and Ct the sine of AC; and then join IK and OL NowHF, OB, GM, CL are all perpendicular to the plane ADDB. And HD, GK, OL, the all in the same plane ADGC. Therefore, the right-angled triangles HHD, CKK, ODL, having the equal angles HDF, CKK OLB, see further. And CK-NOM CI COM; that is, as the sine of the hypotenuse: rad:: sine of a leg - sine of its opposite angle. For OM is the sine of the arc GC, which therefore the angle CAB. Both, LB DF+; BO: FH; that is, as the sine of a leg: radius : tangent of the other leg: tangent of its opposite angle, J, E. D. Hence it follows: that the first of the angles of any oblique spherical triangle ACD (_this_, o^2), letto one ano- they, directly, as the sines of the opposite sides. Hence it also follows, that, in right-angled spherical triangles, having the same perpendicular, the sine of the base will be to each other, inversely, as the tangents of the angles at the base.
